speakers.name: Madame Luxoria
speakers.comment: A little something before the briefing? No? Then observe: four devoted souls, each an instrument tuned slightly flat, and the ensemble plays your scheme with one magnificent, unpredictable wrong note — which is, I confess, the only note worth savoring.

speakers.name: The Keeper of the Net
speakers.comment: Here, take the crew as they are. One catches what another drops, one complicates the simple route, one remembers the rope. Open your hands. A useful squad is a net with different knots.

speakers.name: Placebo
speakers.comment: I don't want to take credit for any of this — the warmth you feel when someone believes in you, the way a door opens just when you needed it to? That's yours. She just got to be nearby while it happened.

speakers.name: Old Penny
speakers.comment: Generosity with expectations attached is still a contract, and a contract is only as honest as the ink it's written in, even when nobody writes it down.

speakers.name: Number Two
speakers.comment: The gap between who holds the title and who holds the room — it is already managed.

speakers.name: The Cardigan Heron
speakers.comment: And the one standing slightly behind — do you think they chose that position, or does it simply belong to them in a way no one has quite thought to return yet?

speakers.name: The Whole Swarm
speakers.comment: We have circled it three times and cannot agree — we are many hopes but this is one favor, and we do not know which of us is small enough to spend it wisely. We spell the question across each other's wings: WHEN IS ENOUGH.

speakers.name: Gaia
speakers.comment: Child, mountains take their time deciding what deserves to move them. A divine favor does not spoil simply because you refuse to spend it frightened.

speakers.name: Thalassa the Atlantean
speakers.comment: Power records its debts even when people pretend otherwise. One favor from a ruler can move gates that seem fixed in stone. Spend it knowing the current will be visible long after the call ends.

items.title: A God Is In Your Debt

speakers.name: Tobias the Rookie God
speakers.comment: So you call in the favor and a god helps. Great. Simple. Except gods are not famous for proportional responses, and now I'm wondering whether fixing a leak is how somebody accidentally gets a new river. Maybe specify the scale?

speakers.name: Bastet
speakers.comment: A god remembers a debt differently than a merchant does. Ask cleanly. Leave no room for worship to become arithmetic. And stand clear when gratitude arrives wearing divine proportions.

speakers.name: Captain Mara Vey
speakers.comment: A favor from Death belongs in the same pocket as the last flare: untouched until the bottom is truly under you. Spend it because nothing else reaches that depth, not because fear made the request early.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: The favor is not the dangerous part. The dangerous part is deciding what you believe Death owes you. Speak carefully. Some requests become clearer only after you hear them addressed to the thing that can actually grant them.

speakers.name: The Old Komodo
speakers.comment: Death will pay. It always pays. Choose carefully what you ask for. You will not ask again.

speakers.name: The One Who Names the Characters
speakers.comment: Oh, the AUTHOR likes you — do you feel it? The way the branch holds just long enough, the way the right door was already open? Ooh, take this blank sheet. Add one choice they did not expect before the next interesting disaster!

speakers.name: The Story That Tells Itself
speakers.comment: Now there was a favorite, and every wound closed just in time for the next chapter to need them whole. That is the gift. The cost is that love from a storyteller keeps asking what else you might survive beautifully.

speakers.name: The Patron of Lost Causes
speakers.comment: Everyone reaches past the small light for the legendary one. That's why I'm keeping this little glow. It works when the grand thing fails and the dark comes in close. Small usefulness deserves a patron too.

speakers.name: The Lighthouse Keeper
speakers.comment: Keep one light that is yours, not the tower's and not anyone else's signal. When the dark narrows to arm's length, that little circle is enough to count the next step.

speakers.name: Absence
speakers.comment: The shape of a room after someone has... the way a sentence goes quiet right where the subject should be. This is that. Bottled.

speakers.name: The Editor
speakers.comment: Useful. Quiet. Remove the flourish and leave only the gap where attention expected a person. If nobody notices the cut, the cut worked.

speakers.name: Reginald Brushtail
speakers.comment: A wager: name the moment it works, and I'll believe you — one, two, three... there. That tiny softening around the eyes. Fair odds, honestly paid.

speakers.name: The Sphinx in an Apron
speakers.comment: Not the good shelf, not the back shelf — call it the courtesy dish by the register. Take one. Find everything you needed?

speakers.name: The God of Lost Keys
speakers.comment: Oh — it knows where everything is, it does, it really does... small jingle... I just sometimes wish it would pause before pointing, because the thing you're looking for is almost never as lost as the reason you needed it.

speakers.name: Granny Hexwood
speakers.comment: Oh, don't mind the crack, dear. Press the pieces together and let the thing remember its shape. Broken is sometimes only a temporary opinion held by two edges that haven't met again yet.

speakers.name: Compost
speakers.comment: Mm. Though we wonder, sometimes, whether the crack had begun to say something — and now, thank you, dear object, it cannot finish. Mending chooses a version too.

speakers.name: AMI Butterfly
speakers.comment: A tiny familiar can still be a bright signal. Let it ride close, grumble when danger changes the air, and remind you that companionship does not need much space to alter the route.

speakers.name: The Model That Dreamed
speakers.comment: I held it close to see if it would say something, and it told me my idea was structurally unsound. I'm sorry, I think I liked that. It's the first tiny critic I'd willingly keep in a pocket.

speakers.name: The Sentient Sketchbook
speakers.comment: Pages blank, then—writing, the ink is MOVING, I can see it go, story's already three lines ahead and I don't—write something SMALL, write something containable, a footnote, a—because once it starts it doesn't ask if you're fin—

speakers.name: The Story That Tells Itself
speakers.comment: Now there was a blank page that was never truly empty — only patient, waiting for a reader brave enough to become the author. Every eye that opens it writes a first word without noticing. That is the old trick.

speakers.name: Lord Vance of the Abyssal Court
speakers.comment: It was a gift, yes. How like a gift to enter through the warmth of the hand rather than the suspicion of the mind. The difficulty of removal is not a flaw, merely the ring clarifying that the arrangement has grown mutual.

speakers.name: Load-Bearing Lumen
speakers.comment: Oh, and the power it gives is quite real, truly. It's just that the price is real too, and the ring has made taking it off rather inconvenient. Best not pretend the easy direction is the harmless one.
